The Wadandi, also spelt Wardandi, are an Aboriginal people of the southwest corner of Western Australia, along the coast from Geographe Bay to Cape Leeuwin, around present day Busselton and Margaret River. They are one of the fourteen language groups of the Noongar. Their name is often said to mean saltwater people.

Their neighbours were the Bibulman to the southeast and the Pinjarup to the north. The coast gave fish, shellfish and whales that washed ashore, and the forests behind gave game and plant food.

Settlers arrived at Augusta and the Vasse in the early 1830s, soon after the founding of the Swan River Colony, and conflict followed. The map shows the Wadandi from 1600 to 1815. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
